title: Claude Cowork and chat come together for Enterprise
summary: Claude chat and Cowork are unified into one experience on web, desktop, and mobile for Enterprise customers. Conversations start as chat and move code or file tasks into a cloud environment that keeps running when the laptop closes, with chats, projects, connectors, skills, and plugins carried over. Agentic work runs in isolated cloud VMs with network access off by default, and admins gain an Efficient mode (Sonnet/Haiku), role-based model access, spend limits, and pooled budgets, with SSO and the Compliance API still applying.

title: Expanding Claude for Nonprofits
summary: A new Claude for Nonprofits plugin of skills and connectors, built with about 30 nonprofits, is auto-installed at no extra cost for nonprofits on Team and Enterprise plans. It covers small-team capacity for marketing, hiring, and board work, setup with a data map and AI policy, and the fundraising lifecycle. The Claude Corps fellowship will be extended via Taproot to match pro bono consultants, and admins control access and connectors with no training on organization data by default.

title: Claude Security now scans continuously and tracks fixes
summary: The latest version of Claude Security, a vulnerability scanner, is in public beta for Claude Enterprise. It runs a baseline scan of connected repos, then risk-based rescans of code changes, marks findings fixed when a fix ships, and reopens them if they reappear. Findings are prioritized by attacker reachability with severity ratings and attack-path explanations, and an API, webhooks, and an MCP connector for Claude.ai and Claude Code are available under role-based permissions.

title: Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop
summary: This Claude Platform guide explains how to merge many specialist subagents into one main agent loop, recommending one model with one tool loop and on-demand skills plus tool search for domain knowledge. Subagents remain useful for context bloat, parallel work, or tool-selection conflicts, but a single agent with skills often delivered better quality, lower cost, and lower latency (one customer was about 2x faster). The suggested migration is to build a small eval and fold in one subagent at a time, and a migration kit is included.

title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
summary: Anthropic describes Scion, its in-house source control system that replaces git for its monorepo, along with the Antique code review tool. Migrated in about five months, it keeps history server-side so clients fetch only needed files, cutting CI checkouts from minutes to seconds with a 200x smaller CPU and memory footprint. Anthropic says Claude-driven development raised daily merges from about 2,500 to over 30,000, making human-scale tooling the bottleneck, and it is not a general git replacement but shares ideas for git platforms to adopt.

title: Introducing Claude Duet
summary: Claude Duet is a research preview of a proactive agent app on iOS, Android, and claude.ai, included in Pro and Max with a US waitlist first. It sends a morning brief, checks connected apps every few hours, messages only when attention is needed, and keeps working in its own VM when devices are off, with 6,000+ connectors and plugins. Approval is required before sending, paying, signing, or deleting, trading and moving money between accounts are off-limits, and Anthropic notes it is early and may misjudge urgency, with background checks counting against shared usage limits.
